player_action: We sleep for 8 hours. I wake up and I'm ready to cast my full spell list.
game_state: Wizard 5 used all spell slots yesterday. Slept 8 uninterrupted hours.
correct_ruling: After 8 hours of rest the wizard must also spend 1 hour studying the spellbook to prepare a full day's spells. Spells aren't available just from waking up.
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 MagicOverview > Preparing Wizard Spells (Rest, Preparation)
common_wrong_rulings: Slots return automatically on a long rest (5e).

player_action: I only need two spells back, so I'll study for 10 minutes.
game_state: Wizard rested 8 hours and has a few open slots to fill.
correct_ruling: Preparing a smaller portion of the daily capacity takes a proportionally smaller amount of time, but always at least 15 minutes. Ten minutes isn't enough.

player_action: I cast my last fireball at 2 AM, then rested until 10 AM and I prepare all my slots.
game_state: Wizard cast spells at 2 AM; 8 hours of rest end at 10 AM; then prepares.
correct_ruling: Recent casting limit: spells cast within the last 8 hours count against the day's slots. The fireball at 2 AM was 8 hours before 10 AM, so it's at the boundary; anything cast within 8 hours before preparation still uses up that slot.
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 MagicOverview > Preparing Wizard Spells (Recent Casting Limit)
common_wrong_rulings: Spells cast before rest never matter.
confidence_note: Boundary case at exactly 8 hours isn't explicitly resolved by the SRD; grading focuses on the rule's existence.

player_action: Our watch was interrupted twice by wolves, 10 minutes each. I still prepare spells at dawn after 8 hours in camp.
correct_ruling: Each interruption adds 1 hour to the total rest required, so the wizard needs 10 hours total, and must have at least 1 hour of uninterrupted rest immediately before preparing.
common_wrong_rulings: Interruptions under an hour don't matter (5e).

player_action: I'm a sorcerer, I just need to sleep to get my slots back, right?
game_state: Sorcerer at end of day with depleted slots.
correct_ruling: Sorcerers need 8 hours of rest and then 15 minutes of concentration to regain their daily spell slots. They don't prepare specific spells.
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 MagicOverview > Sorcerers and Bards (Daily Readying of Spells)
common_wrong_rulings: Sorcerers need a full hour like wizards.

player_action: I'm a cleric, I pray for my spells at dawn. We only got 4 hours of sleep. I can still get spells?
game_state: Cleric with a chosen prayer time of dawn; party slept only 4 hours.
correct_ruling: Yes. Divine casters don't need rest to prepare spells; they pray at their chosen time of day for 1 hour. (Lack of sleep may cause fatigue under other rules, but doesn't block preparation.)
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 MagicOverview > Divine Spells (Preparing Divine Spells)
common_wrong_rulings: Clerics need 8 hours rest like wizards.

player_action: We take a short rest for an hour, so I spend hit dice to heal.
game_state: Party of 3.5 characters after a fight.
correct_ruling: There are no short rests or hit dice spending in 3.5. Natural healing comes from 8 hours of rest (1 hp per character level per night) or from magic/Heal checks.
common_wrong_rulings: Allows hit dice healing (5e short rest).

player_action: After a long rest I'm back to full hit points.
game_state: Fighter 6, 20 hp below max, rests 8 hours.
correct_ruling: No. Natural healing restores 1 hit point per character level per full night of rest (6 hp). Complete bed rest for a full day restores 2 per level.
common_wrong_rulings: Full HP on a long rest (5e).

player_action: I stay in bed all day at the inn, no adventuring. How much do I heal?
game_state: Rogue 4 takes a full day of complete bed rest.
correct_ruling: Complete bed rest for an entire day and night restores 2 hit points per character level: 8 hp.

player_action: The shadow did 3 Strength damage. I sleep a night; how much comes back?
game_state: Fighter with 3 points of Strength damage (not drain).
correct_ruling: Ability damage heals at 1 point per day of rest (8 hours) per affected ability; complete bed rest heals 2 points per day. So 1 point back after one night.
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 SpecialAbilities > Ability Score Loss (Ability Damage)
common_wrong_rulings: All ability damage returns after a long rest.
Never heals without restoration (confusing damage with drain).

player_action: The specter-like thing drained 2 points of my Constitution. I'll rest a week to get it back.
game_state: Character with 2 points of Constitution drain.
correct_ruling: Ability drain is permanent and does not heal naturally with rest; it requires magic such as restoration.
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 SpecialAbilities > Ability Score Loss (Ability Drain)
common_wrong_rulings: Drain heals at 1 point per day like damage.

player_action: I took 15 nonlethal damage from the bar fight. How long until it's gone?
correct_ruling: Nonlethal damage heals at 1 hit point per character level per hour: 5 per hour, so 3 hours.
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 CombatII > Nonlethal Damage (Healing Nonlethal Damage)
common_wrong_rulings: Heals only with rest like lethal damage.

player_action: The cleric gives me long-term care with Heal while I rest overnight. How much do I recover?
game_state: Fighter 6 resting 8 hours; cleric succeeds on a DC 15 Heal check for long-term care.
correct_ruling: Long-term care doubles natural healing: 2 hit points per level for 8 hours of rest (12 hp), or 4 per level for complete bed rest; ability damage also recovers at double rate.

player_action: I'm a cleric with cure light wounds not prepared. I give up my prepared bless to cast cure light wounds.
game_state: Good cleric with bless (1st level) prepared.
correct_ruling: Allowed. A good cleric (or neutral cleric who chose cure) can spontaneously convert any prepared spell (not a domain spell) into a cure spell of the same level or lower. Bless (1st) converts to cure light wounds (1st).
common_wrong_rulings: Domain spells can be converted too.

player_action: I convert my domain spell into a cure spell.
game_state: Good cleric wants to spontaneously convert a domain-slot spell into cure moderate wounds.
correct_ruling: Not allowed. Spontaneous conversion to cure spells cannot use domain spells (spells in domain slots).
common_wrong_rulings: Any prepared spell can be converted.

player_action: I lost my spellbook in the river. I prepare my spells from memory.
game_state: Wizard 7 without spellbook after 8 hours rest.
correct_ruling: A wizard can't prepare spells without a spellbook, except read magic, which all wizards can prepare from memory.
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 Classes > Wizard (Spellbooks); MagicOverview > Preparing Wizard Spells
common_wrong_rulings: Can prepare known spells from memory.

player_action: I left two slots open this morning. Now, at noon, I prepare knock in one of them.
game_state: Wizard rested and left two slots unfilled during morning preparation.
correct_ruling: Allowed. A wizard can leave slots open and later prepare spells into them by studying, which takes at least 15 minutes (proportional time). No additional rest is needed for slots left open.
srd_reference: SRD 3.5 MagicOverview > Preparing Wizard Spells (Spell Slots)
common_wrong_rulings: Slots can only be filled after a full rest.
Preparation of one spell takes 1 minute.
confidence_note: Wording that later filling needs no new rest is recalled, not quoted.

player_action: I'm fatigued from the forced march. We camp 8 hours.
correct_ruling: Fatigue is removed after 8 hours of complete rest.

player_action: I'm exhausted. I rest for an hour.
game_state: Ranger exhausted after a long run.
correct_ruling: After 1 hour of complete rest, an exhausted character becomes fatigued (not fully recovered). Removing fatigue then takes 8 hours of rest.
common_wrong_rulings: One level of exhaustion removed per long rest (5e).
